<title>Brass Console: render the blob-integrity readout and did:web hosting flag</title>
<description>
<issue id="e95731ec-2922-4ebe-9ec4-27c836063e28" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-474/blob-observability-ownership-loss-is-indistinguishable-from-byte-loss">MM-474</issue> (PR #441) added three operator readouts to the API. None of them are rendered by the admin-companion app yet, so they are JSON an operator has to curl for — which is most of the gap <issue id="e95731ec-2922-4ebe-9ec4-27c836063e28" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-474/blob-observability-ownership-loss-is-indistinguishable-from-byte-loss">MM-474</issue> set out to close.

Same shape as the <issue id="6a22b24b-7904-49cc-b5dd-e4d5386b8b54" href="https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-472/blob-gc-destroys-the-blobs-of-any-account-whose-reconcile-fails">MM-472</issue> → #439 split: the relay-side signal landed first, the console-side rendering followed separately.

## The fields

| Endpoint | Fields | What they mean |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `GET /v1/admin/health` | `storage.blobUnownedCount`, `storage.blobUnownedBytes` | Stored blobs no account claims. Expect ~0 — GC drops a physical row with its last owner, so a row is unowned only between two statements. A standing value means bytes intact, ownership gone. |
| `GET /v1/accounts/:id/storage` | `uploadedBlobCount`, `uploadedBlobBytes` | Physical rows naming this account as uploader, beside the ownership figures. |
| `GET /v1/admin/accounts` | `didWebHosting` | Whether Custos serves this account's did:web document. |

## Suggested scope

1. **Status screen** — surface `blobUnownedCount`/`Bytes` in the storage block. This one is genuinely alertable: it needs no threshold tuning (~0 is the real baseline), and unlike a stale `blobGc.completedAt` it fires while the sweep is still running on schedule — the exact condition that made the original loss invisible for six hours. Worth a distinct treatment from the ordinary blob counts, not another neutral row.
2. **Account detail / storage** — show the uploaded figures beside the owned ones. Divergence here is **not** a fault by itself: blobs are content-addressed and shared, so owned-not-uploaded and uploaded-not-owned both occur normally. Present it as a second reading, not a warning — a red badge on benign sharing would train the operator to ignore it.
3. **Account list/detail** — a `didWebHosting` indicator. The flag gates a serve path that 404s indistinguishably from an unknown host when off, so its value is telling "not hosted" apart from "broken".

## Constraints

* Brass Console brief: `apps/admin-companion/PRODUCT.md` + `DESIGN.md` (terminal-native, cool-slate/gold, monospace-forward — **not** the Obsign register). Target `/impeccable` at `apps/admin-companion` so it loads the right brief.
* Status never by colour alone (WCAG 2.2 AAA): pair any integrity state with text + icon + position, the way the sweep rows already name `failed <n>` versus `stale`.
* Older relays predating these fields must degrade to "not reported" rather than failing the screen — the same posture #439 took for the sweep `errors` field.
</description>

# Linear Development Workflow

This skill manages the full lifecycle of working on a Linear issue: from picking it up through opening a PR.

## Starting Work on an Issue

When the user indicates they want to work on a Linear issue (e.g., "Let's work on MM-42"):

1. **Parse the issue identifier** from the user's message. The pattern is `MM-` followed by a number.

2. **Fetch the issue details** from Linear using the `get_issue` tool with the parsed identifier. Display a brief summary to the user: title, description (truncated if long), priority, and any existing labels.

3. **Update the issue in Linear:**
   - Set the status to **"In Progress"**
   - Assign it to **"me"** (the authenticated user)

   Use the `save_issue` tool with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Progress"`, and `assignee: "me"`.

4. **Create a git branch from a fresh base** using the issue's suggested branch name:
   - The `get_issue` response includes a `branchName` field — use that as the branch name.
   - **Fetch first, then branch from the remote tip — never from a possibly-stale local HEAD:**
     `git fetch origin main && git checkout -b <branchName> origin/main`
     A stale base silently duplicates work that already merged (hours lost rebuilding an already-shipped backend is the known failure mode).
   - If the branch already exists locally, check it out, then run `git log --oneline <branchName>..origin/main` and surface to the user how far behind the base is.

5. **Verify sibling work is in the base.** If the issue depends on or overlaps sibling issues already marked Done in Linear, confirm their PRs are actually present in the branch base (e.g. `git log --oneline origin/main | grep -i mm-nnn`, or check for the files/routes they added) before concluding any related feature is "missing". **"Linear says Done but the code isn't here" is a hard stop-and-verify signal — it almost always means your base is stale, not that the feature needs building.**

6. **Confirm to the user** what happened: issue assigned, status updated, branch created/checked out (and from which base commit). Then ask what they'd like to tackle first, or summarize the issue so they can dive in.

## Opening a PR (Auto-transition to "In Review")

When the user asks to open a PR, create a pull request, or you detect that a PR is being created for a branch associated with a Linear issue:

1. **Identify the Linear issue** from the current branch name. Linear branch names typically contain the issue identifier (e.g., `malpercio/mm-42-fix-the-thing`). Extract the `MM-XXX` portion.

2. **Create the PR** as the user requests (follow normal PR creation workflow).

3. **After the PR is successfully created**, update the Linear issue:
   - Set the status to **"In Review"**
   - Attach the PR URL as a link on the issue using the `links` field in `save_issue`

   Use `save_issue` with the issue's `id`, `state: "In Review"`, and `links: [{"url": "<pr-url>", "title": "Pull Request"}]`.

4. **Confirm** to the user that the issue has been moved to "In Review" and the PR link has been attached.

## Important Notes

- Always fetch the issue first to confirm it exists and get the full `id` (UUID) needed for updates.
- If the issue is already "In Progress" and assigned, skip those updates and just create the branch.
- If branch creation fails (e.g., uncommitted changes), inform the user and suggest next steps rather than silently failing.
- The PR-to-"In Review" transition should happen automatically whenever a PR is opened during a session where the user started work on a Linear issue. Track the active issue identifier throughout the session.

Full picture in hand. Here's the key design judgment before I write code:

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`

Closes [MM-476](https://linear.app/malpercio/issue/MM-476/brass-console-render-the-blob-integrity-readout-and-didweb-hosting).

MM-474 (#441) added three operator readouts to the API. None were rendered by the admin-companion app, so they were JSON an operator had to curl for — which was most of the gap MM-474 set out to close. Same shape as the MM-472 → #439 split: relay-side signal first, console-side rendering separately.

## What each one does

**Status → Storage: `unowned blobs`.** Stored blob rows no account claims. This is the one genuinely alertable figure on the screen and the only one carrying a verdict, so it does not sit in the neutral run of counts — it gets its own named row plus, when a population is actually reported, a stated consequence beneath the grid. It needs no threshold tuning (collection drops a physical row together with its last owner, so ~0 is the real baseline), and it is strictly more sensitive than the `blob GC` sweep line beside it: staleness can only report a sweep that *stopped*, while this fires with the sweep running exactly on schedule — the condition that once kept a real loss invisible for six hours.

**Account detail: `uploaded blobs`.** The physical rows naming the account as first uploader, beside the ownership figures the rest of the panel reports. Deliberately verdict-free and unmarked, with a note saying why: blobs are content-addressed and shared, so owned-not-uploaded and uploaded-not-owned both occur normally, and a badge on that benign divergence would train the operator to ignore badges.

**Account row: did:web hosting.** `served here` / `not served here` / `not reported`, in the same muted register as the quota readout — hosting off is a configuration, not a fault. Rendered **only** for did:web accounts: the question does not arise for did:plc (whose document lives on plc.directory), and answering it on every row would bury the rows where the answer means something.

## The degradation choice worth reviewing

All three degrade to `not reported` on an older relay, per the posture #439 took for the sweep `errors` field — but by a **different mechanism**, and that difference is the main design decision here.

`errors` could safely `serde(default)` a missing value to `0`, because 0 there means "no failures". For these three, the zero/false value is itself a meaningful reading — `blobUnownedCount: 0` is precisely this readout's all-clear — so defaulting would fabricate an all-clear an older relay never gave. They are therefore modelled as `Option`/nullable end-to-end, and the three outcomes (`not reported` / `none` / a marked line) are never collapsed. Serde maps a missing field to `None` on an `Option` without an attribute; the Rust deserialization tests pin that, including the older-relay JSON.

That caught a second real bug — the alarm row's `.dd--alarm` rule (specificity 0,1,0) was losing to the existing `.facts dd` rule (0,1,1) and rendering in plain ink. Worth noting that the *meaning* survived anyway, because the value itself reads `ownership lost !` — the AAA "never by colour alone" rule doing its job.

Done. [PR #452](https://github.com/malpercio-dev/ezpds/pull/452) is open; MM-476 is In Review with the PR attached.

## What shipped

All three MM-474 readouts now render, each with the treatment the issue asked for:

- **Status → Storage** ([status/+page.svelte](apps/admin-companion/src/routes/status/+page.svelte)) names `unowned blobs` in its own row, with a stated consequence beneath the grid when a population is reported. Distinct from the neutral counts, as asked.
- **Account detail** ([account/+page.svelte](apps/admin-companion/src/routes/account/+page.svelte)) shows `uploaded blobs` beside the owned figures, verdict-free, with a note explaining why divergence is normal.
- **Account row** ([AccountRow.svelte](apps/admin-companion/src/lib/components/ui/AccountRow.svelte)) states did:web hosting — only on did:web rows.

## The judgment call worth your review

The degradation posture matches #439's *intent* but not its *mechanism*. `errors` could safely default a missing value to `0` because 0 there means "no failures". Here **0 is the all-clear** — `blobUnownedCount: 0` is exactly what a healthy server reports — so defaulting would fabricate an all-clear an old relay never gave. I modelled all three as `Option`/nullable end-to-end instead, keeping `not reported` / `none` / alarm as three distinct outcomes. If you'd rather they matched #439 literally, that's the line to push back on.

## Two real bugs the verification caught

Worth flagging because they argue for keeping both checks in the loop:

1. `pnpm check` found an `AccountListEntry` literal in `flags.test.ts` missing the new required field — the unit tests passed regardless, since vitest doesn't typecheck.
2. Driving the harness found my alarm-tone rule silently losing a CSS specificity contest (`.dd--alarm` at 0,1,0 vs the existing `.facts dd` at 0,1,1). The tests couldn't have caught it. Notably the *meaning* survived anyway — the value reads `ownership lost !` on its own — which is the never-colour-alone rule earning its keep.

Verification: 90 Rust tests, 195 frontend tests, clippy clean, `pnpm check` 0 errors, and both harness scenarios driven live. Harness fixtures seed the healthy zero, the degraded population, and a did:web account per relay, so all three states are reachable without a simulator.
